title: Typed history publication republishes the whole consolidated commit lane
wanted_capability: Incremental typed-history publication in which ordinary HEAD advances publish commit-document deltas derived corpus-side from verified predecessor and successor manifests. Force-pushes and ancestry changes must select an explicit full-replacement recovery path. Overlay and code-selector revisions must evolve independently from a committed activation journal so selector-only drift does not republish commit documents. The governing proposal is design/daemon-runtime/incremental-history-publication.md.
missing_primitive: Corpus-derived commit-lane delta publication with explicit full-replacement recovery, an overlay-revision ledger for committed activations, and rooted vector tombstoning across overlapping generation inventories.
fallback_used: No-op currency checks prevent unchanged source trees from repeatedly activating, and operators can pause high-volume history publication and embedding. Genuine HEAD advances still pay the whole-lane publication cost.
notes: The proposed design preserves complete producer snapshots and derives deltas only after corpus-side verification. Its implementation gates include force-push recovery, crash-safe overlay revisions, rooted vector retention, sustained-cadence soak testing, and cross-restart coverage persistence. Earlier currency fixes removed no-op self-amplification but did not change the per-commit worst case.
